cards.question: How is malignant hyperthermia treated?
cards.answer: Stop all volatile agents and suxamethonium, switch to TIVA, remove the vaporiser without delaying to change the circuit or machine (charcoal filters if available), hyperventilate with 100% oxygen, give IV dantrolene 2–2.5 mg/kg (max 300 mg per dose) every 10 min to effect — totals above 10 mg/kg may be needed, cool actively, and treat hyperkalaemia, acidosis and arrhythmias (AAGBI 2020).

cards.question: Why is suxamethonium contraindicated in Duchenne and Becker muscular dystrophy?
cards.answer: Even sub-clinical dystrophinopathy can precipitate rhabdomyolysis and hyperkalaemic cardiac arrest after suxamethonium or prolonged volatile exposure — TIVA with non-depolarising NMBs is mandatory.

cards.question: What are the airway considerations in Down syndrome?
cards.answer: Macroglossia, narrow nasopharynx, subglottic stenosis (use a smaller ETT than predicted) and atlanto-axial instability (careful neck positioning, neutral head) — plus a high prevalence of congenital cardiac disease and obstructive sleep apnoea.
